newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU's COCERAL to raise cereals crop forecast - source.
newsitem.headline: EU's COCERAL to raise cereals crop forecast - source.

text.p: The European Union grain trade association COCERAL will raise its 1996 cereals crop forecast upwards on Thursday, a trade source told Reuters.
"The crop forecast is expected to be raised significantly when COCERAL has completed today's re-evaluation of the figures," the source said.
COCERAL forecast on September 23 that the 1996 EU grain crop would be 198.49 million tonnes.
That compared with a figure of 200.7 million tonnes compiled by the European Commission from national estimates.
A COCERAL official declined to comment. "We are revising our figures today and we will be discussing them on Friday," the official said.

Commission experts said on Thursday that they had adjusted the 200.7 million tonnes given by member states downwards to allow for over-estimates in some member states. The new figure has not been released.
"There is a tendency for national estimates to be too high and we remain cautious about the final crop figure," an official said.
On Wednesday the French cereals intervention agency ONIC said it had raised its soft wheat crop estimate to 34.3 million tonnes from an earlier forecast of 33.8 million.

The British National Farmers Union estimated last week that Britain's 1996 grain harvest would be 24.09 million tonnes, up from last year's 21.86 million, with oats and other cereals at 650,000 tonnes compared with last year's 720,000 tonnes.
